meaning:
τόκος, -ου, ὁ
(τίκτω), [in LXX for נֶשֶׁךְ, etc. ;]
(a) a bringing forth, birth;
(b) offspring. Metaphorical, of the produce of money lent out, interest, usury (cf. Merch. of Venice, I, iii, "a breed of barren metal "): Mat.25:27, Luk.19:23 (Soph., Plat., al.).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
Then why didn’t you deposit my money in the bank, and at my coming, I might have earned interest on it?’
